newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian province plans to sue tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: Canadian province plans to sue tobacco companies.

text.p: The Canadian province of British Columbia said on Wednesday it intends to sue tobacco companies in a bid to recover health-care costs for smoking-related illnesses.
Legal experts believed the lawsuit, similar to 15 already launched by U.S. states, would be the first of its kind by a governmental body outside the United States.
British Columbia Health Minister Joy MacPhail said the lawsuit was part of an intensified campaign by the province to fight smoking.

"I have asked the lawyers in my ministry ... to pursue all options around taking the tobacco companies to court for the health-care costs imposed upon our system as a result of tobacco use," MacPhail said in remarks distributed by her ministry.
"We will be pursuing all our legal options to the full limit."

British Columbia, like other Canadian provinces, provides universal health care. Fred Bass of the British Columbia Doctors Stop Smoking Project told the Canadian Press news agency that smoking costs the provincial health-care system an estimated C$420 million to C$560 million (US$311 million to US$415 million a year.
A ministry spokesman said no date has been set for the lawsuit to be filed, although the province had decided in principle to proceed with the case. "Clearly the intention is to sue," he said.
The ministry did not release the names of the companies to be targeted by the lawsuit.

Richard Daynard, chairman of the Tobacco Products Liability Project at Northeastern Law School in Boston, said he believes that British Columbia would be the first governmental agency outside the United States to sue the tobacco industry to recoup health-care costs of smokers.
"This should send shivers down the spine of tobacco industry executives who think the only threat is in the United States," Daynard said.

So far 15 states have sued cigarette companies seeking reimbursement of Medicaid costs and last week Illinois said it planned to become the 16th state. San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Jose and 10 other counties in California have also sued the industry and Erie County, New York, which includes the city of Buffalo, also plans to sue.
